einer Seits

2., der hiesige Fürstl. forst Inspector Carl Titz andrer Seits.

Comparenten sind denen Subforestis persönlich bekannt u befinden sich um dem Zustande gerichtliche hinndlungen gültig zu woll ziehen.

Dieselben verlautbaren freywillig u wohlbedächtig folgenden unter sich getroffenen im

§ I. Es verleihen nemlich Sr. Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht von dem hiesigen Trąbczyner vorwerk Acker dem ForstInspector Carl Titz 5 Hufen sage fünf hufen Magdeburg. u. zwar suter denen Vorwerksgebünden von dem Wege ab welcher nach Podbiele führt bis an den Mühlen Graben mit Inbe griff des neben den Stallungen liegenden Obst Gartens von jezt ab auf eine merwührende Zeiten in Erbzinß.

§. II. Der forstInspector Seite

stell zahlt an Einkaufsgeld für jede Hufe 300 rt schreiben drey hundert Rthaler mithin für fünf hufen Magdeburg 1500 rt. schreibe Eintausendfünf hundert Rthaler und zwar mit der einen hälfte a 750 rt schreibe Siebenhundertfünfzig Rtheler im Johanni dieses Jahre und mit der andern halfte a 750 rt schreibe Siebenhundert fünfzig Rthaler mit Johanni des künftigen Jahres 1806 baar u. in guten preußl. Courant.

§. III. Der forst Inspector Titz macht sich verbindlich für die staaquirirte Stelle von Johannis dieses Jahres ab einen immerwähren

renden fährl. Erbzinß der und erhöhet oder vermindet wer dendurf, pro hufe Magdeburg mit 15 rt schreibe fünfzehn Rthaler mithin für fünf hufen 75 rt schreibe fünft und Siebenzig Rthaler in Courant und zwar jährlich in zweyen Raten zu Weynachten und Johannis jedesmal mit 37 rt 12 gg schreibe Sieben u. dreyßig Rthaler 12 gg. post numerando baar zu bezahlen.

§. IV. von der zweiten haltte der Einkaufs geldes der 75 ortum, werden bis zum zahlungs Tage fünf pro hut zum en entrichtet

§. V.

S. V.

Seid Etablissement muß stitz sich auf eigene Kosten ohne daß er hiezu weder von jezt auch für die zukunft holtz oder sonstige Bau hulfe erhält selbst bewürken.

§. VI. Ausser diesem kam ren Erbzinße verpflichtet sich ErbPachter für sich und seine Nachfolger im besitze dieser aaquirten Stelle, von diesen fünf hufen

alle und jede Königl. Steuern sowie die Competenz fürs Kloster Ląd u die abgaben an die Gräßlichkeit Rauchfangsegeld, faurage fieferung und was sonst vor lommt, ohne alle Ausnahme zu berichtigen, ohne hiefür en

einen Erlaß wur nem Erbzinse zu machen oder zu erhalten.

§. VII. Erbpächter muß sein getrunkam Bier und Brandtwein mit dem Herrschaft, frage oder Braun und Vormundthännte nehmen und im Contraventione Fall für jeden eingebrachten Garniec fremden Brandtwein Einen Rthaler und für jede könne fremdes Bier fünf Rthaler Strafe der Grundherrschaft erlegen.

§. VIII. ErbPächter und seine Nachfolger um Biesigge dieser Stelle, sind der Jurisdiction des hiesigen konnen unterworfen, jedoch man allen und

jeden Natural lieferungen und hufe diensten gänzlich und für immerwährende Zeiten befreyet.

§. IX. Dem Erbflichten und seinen Nachfolgern anliesig, steht es frey, diese acquirir te [word?] [word?] An dere durch Verkauf oder vertausch zu vermüßern, jedoch muß solches mit Consens der Grundherr schrift geschehen und bei einer jeden vergleichen bestig Verminderung von dem Kaufgelde udertausch quanto der gehüte Groschen als ein Condemnen an die Grundherrschaft entrichtet werden ben vererbungen an finden und Seiten verwandte dagegen

wird kein Laudemium bezahlt.

§. X. ErbPächter leistet für sich und seine Nachfolger im Besiz auf alle und jede Remissionen bei Un glückfüllen, welche durch Feuer vom Himmel durch Anstekung böser leute, haagelschlag Mißwachs Viehsterben krieg und Pest oder auf irgend eine ander wart entstehen, ganz lich Verzicht, und sell ihnen dieser halb nie eine Entschädigung von der Grundherrschaft uderfrlaß von dem Erbzinße zu statte kommen.

§. XI. Die Wohn und Wirthschafts gebunde muß ErbPächter

und seine Nachfolger um Besiz auf eigene sonsten selbster bauen u. dieselben stets um baulichen Stande erhalten u erhält siezu von der Grundherrschaft weder holz noch sonstige brauchelfe.

§. XII. diesen dieses Contracts und dessen aus fertigung bezahlt der ErbPächter.

§. XIII. So lange ErbPächter u. seine Nachfolger im Bestege dieser Stelle allen obigen verbindlichkeiten nachkommen

wird, wer spricht die Grundherrschaft sie bei ihren Gerechtsamen

überall zu schützen, und

gegen Jeder manns Real Ansprüche zu vertreten.

Sollte aber ErbPächter über seine Nachfolger diese Stelle verwüsten, oder den jährlichen Erbzinß durch länger als zwey Jahre rükständig bleiben so hört alsdann dieser Erbkauffs Contract auf u die Grundherrschaft wird berechtigt seyn diese Stelle anderweit mus güthen.

Sr. Hochfürstl. durch laucht willigen ausdrücklich darin denß Erbpächter auf den Grund dieses Contracts den Besitz Titul von dieser acquirirten Stelle auf seinen Nahmen berichtigen lassen kann. wen

translation.en:
Actum Trąbczyn, the 4th of May 1805. Before the Patrimonial Court here there appeared in person:

1. the Herr Councillor of War and Forests v. Triebenfeld, as the known General Bevollmächtigter [general authorised representative] of His Serene Highness the reigning Prince zu Hohenlohe Ingelfingen, hereditary and judicial lord of the estates here,

on the one part;

2. the Princely Forest Inspector here, Carl Titz, on the other part.

The comparents are personally known to the Subforestis and are found to be in a condition to execute judicial transactions validly.

They declare, freely and after due deliberation, the following, concluded between themselves, in the

irrevocable hereditary quit-rent contract, in no point to be altered, to the protocol:

§ I. Namely, His Most Serene Highness grants in hereditary quit-rent to the Forest Inspector Carl Titz, out of the arable of the demesne farm here at Trąbczyn, 5 Hufen, in words five Hufen Magdeburg [measure], and that [uncertain: below] the demesne-farm buildings, from the road which leads to Podbiele as far as the mill-ditch, including the orchard lying beside the stables, from now on for perpetual times in hereditary quit-rent.

§ II. The Forest Inspector's hold-

ing pays as purchase-money for each Hufe 300 rt, in words three hundred Rthaler, hence for five Hufen Magdeburg 1500 rt, in words one thousand five hundred Rthaler, and that with the one half at 750 rt, in words seven hundred and fifty Rthaler, at Johanni of this year, and with the other half at 750 rt, in words seven hundred and fifty Rthaler, at Johanni of the coming year 1806, in cash and in good Prussian Courant.

§ III. The Forest Inspector Titz binds himself, for the acquired holding, from Johanni of this year onward, to a perpet-

ual annual hereditary quit-rent, which may neither be raised nor diminished, per Hufe Magdeburg of 15 rt, in words fifteen Rthaler, hence for five Hufen 75 rt, in words seventy-five Rthaler, in Courant, and that yearly in two instalments, at Christmas and at Johanni, each time of 37 rt 12 gg, in words thirty-seven Rthaler 12 gg, to be paid in cash post numerando.

§ IV. Of the second half of the purchase-money, [uncertain: the 75 ortum], five per cent shall be paid up to the day of payment.

§ V.

§ V.

He must effect the establishment himself at his own cost, without receiving for this purpose, either now or in future, timber or any other building assistance.

§ VI. Besides this bare hereditary quit-rent, the hereditary lessee binds himself, for himself and his successors in possession of this acquired holding, to discharge from these five Hufen each and every Royal tax, as well as the assessment for the Ląd monastery and the dues to the [uncertain: county / lordship], chimney-money, forage deliveries and whatever else may arise, without any exception, without on this account

to make or to obtain any remission of the hereditary quit-rent.

§ VII. The hereditary lessee must take the beer and brandy for his own consumption from the lordship's [uncertain: brewery or distillery] and [illegible], and in the case of contravention must pay to the ground-lordship as penalty, for every Garniec of foreign brandy brought in, one Rthaler, and for every keg of foreign beer, five Rthaler.

§ VIII. The hereditary lessee and his successors in possession of this holding are subject to the jurisdiction of the court here, however [text lost] all and

every deliveries in kind and Hufe-services entirely and for perpetual times exempt.

§ IX. The hereditary lessee and his successors in possession are at liberty to alienate this acquired [uncertain: word] [uncertain: word] to others by sale or exchange; however, such must be done with the consent of the ground-lordship, and upon each such [uncertain: reduction of possession] the [uncertain: tenth] Groschen of the purchase-money or exchange sum shall be paid to the ground-lordship as a [uncertain: Laudemium]; whereas upon inheritances to children and collateral relatives, on the other hand,

no Laudemium is paid.

§ X. The hereditary lessee, for himself and his successors in possession, wholly renounces each and every remission in cases of misfortune arising through fire from heaven, through arson by evil persons, hail-storm, crop failure, cattle plague, war and pestilence, or in any other manner whatsoever; and on this account no compensation from the ground-lordship, nor any remission of the hereditary quit-rent, shall ever accrue to them.

§ XI. The dwelling and farm buildings must the hereditary lessee

and his successors in possession build themselves at their own [uncertain: cost], and keep the same always in good repair; and he shall receive for this purpose from the ground-lordship neither timber nor any other building assistance.

§ XII. [uncertain: The costs] of this contract and of its engrossment the hereditary lessee shall pay.

§ XIII. So long as the hereditary lessee and his successors in possession of this holding shall fulfil all the above obligations, the ground-lordship promises to protect them in their rights everywhere, and

to defend them against every man's real claims.

Should, however, the hereditary lessee [uncertain: or] his successors lay waste this holding, or remain in arrears with the annual hereditary quit-rent for longer than two years, then this hereditary-purchase contract shall cease, and the ground-lordship shall be entitled to dispose of this holding otherwise.

Both parties promise to keep the foregoing hereditary quit-rent contract firmly and inviolably, and renounce all legal exceptions to be found therein,

in particular the objection of cunning persuasion, of over-hastiness, of an injury sustained above or below the half, of matters agreed otherwise than as set down in writing; and they have now been duly instructed by the court as to the consequences of this renunciation. Peter Friedrich August v. Triebenfeld
Carl Titz

Actum Trąbczyn, the 4th of May 1805. Before the Patrimonial Court here there appeared in person:

1. the Herr Councillor of War and Forests v. Triebenfeld, as the known General Bevollmächtigter [general authorised representative] of His Serene Highness the reigning Prince zu Hohenlohe Ingelfingen, hereditary and judicial lord of the estates here,

on the one part;

2. the Princely Forest Inspector here, Carl Titz, on the other part.

The comparents are personally known to the Subforestis and are found to be in a condition to execute judicial transactions validly.

They declare, freely and after due deliberation, the following, concluded between themselves, in the

irrevocable hereditary quit-rent contract, in no point to be altered, to the protocol:

§ I. Namely, His Most Serene Highness grants in hereditary quit-rent to the Forest Inspector Carl Titz, out of the arable of the demesne farm here at Trąbczyn, 5 Hufen, in words five Hufen Magdeburg [measure], and that [uncertain: below] the demesne-farm buildings, from the road which leads to Podbiele as far as the mill-ditch, including the orchard lying beside the stables, from now on for perpetual times in hereditary quit-rent.

§ II. The Forest Inspector's hold-

ing pays as purchase-money for each Hufe 300 rt, in words three hundred Rthaler, hence for five Hufen Magdeburg 1500 rt, in words one thousand five hundred Rthaler, and that with the one half at 750 rt, in words seven hundred and fifty Rthaler, at Johanni of this year, and with the other half at 750 rt, in words seven hundred and fifty Rthaler, at Johanni of the coming year 1806, in cash and in good Prussian Courant.

§ III. The Forest Inspector Titz binds himself, for the acquired holding, from Johanni of this year onward, to a perpet-

ual annual hereditary quit-rent, which may neither be raised nor diminished, per Hufe Magdeburg of 15 rt, in words fifteen Rthaler, hence for five Hufen 75 rt, in words seventy-five Rthaler, in Courant, and that yearly in two instalments, at Christmas and at Johanni, each time of 37 rt 12 gg, in words thirty-seven Rthaler 12 gg, to be paid in cash post numerando.

§ IV. Of the second half of the purchase-money, [uncertain: the 75 ortum], five per cent shall be paid up to the day of payment.

§ V.

§ V.

He must effect the establishment himself at his own cost, without receiving for this purpose, either now or in future, timber or any other building assistance.

§ VI. Besides this bare hereditary quit-rent, the hereditary lessee binds himself, for himself and his successors in possession of this acquired holding, to discharge from these five Hufen each and every Royal tax, as well as the assessment for the Ląd monastery and the dues to the [uncertain: county / lordship], chimney-money, forage deliveries and whatever else may arise, without any exception, without on this account

to make or to obtain any remission of the hereditary quit-rent.

§ VII. The hereditary lessee must take the beer and brandy for his own consumption from the lordship's [uncertain: brewery or distillery] and [illegible], and in the case of contravention must pay to the ground-lordship as penalty, for every Garniec of foreign brandy brought in, one Rthaler, and for every keg of foreign beer, five Rthaler.

§ VIII. The hereditary lessee and his successors in possession of this holding are subject to the jurisdiction of the court here, however [text lost] all and

every deliveries in kind and Hufe-services entirely and for perpetual times exempt.

§ IX. The hereditary lessee and his successors in possession are at liberty to alienate this acquired [uncertain: word] [uncertain: word] to others by sale or exchange; however, such must be done with the consent of the ground-lordship, and upon each such [uncertain: reduction of possession] the [uncertain: tenth] Groschen of the purchase-money or exchange sum shall be paid to the ground-lordship as a [uncertain: Laudemium]; whereas upon inheritances to children and collateral relatives, on the other hand,

summary_en: Irrevocable hereditary quit-rent contract concluded before the Patrimonial Court at Trąbczyn between Councillor of War and Forests Peter Friedrich August v. Triebenfeld, General Bevollmächtigter of the Fürst zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, and the princely Forest Inspector Carl Titz, granting Titz five Magdeburg Hufen of the Trąbczyn demesne arable towards Podbiele and the mill-ditch, with orchard, for 1500 Rthaler purchase-money in two Johanni instalments and 75 Rthaler yearly quit-rent, plus taxes, Ląd monastery assessment, beer and brandy monopoly, Laudemium on sale, and no remission for misfortune.
summary_de: Unwiderruflicher Erbzinskontrakt, geschlossen vor dem Patrimonialgericht zwischen dem Kriegs- und Forstrat v. Triebenfeld als General-Bevollmächtigtem des Fürsten zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen und dem fürstlichen Forstinspektor Carl Titz über 5 Hufen magdeburgisch Ackerland des Vorwerks Trąbczyn, von der Straße nach Podbiele bis zum Mühlgraben samt Obstgarten. Kaufgeld 300 Rthl je Hufe, zusammen 1500 Rthl in zwei Raten zu Johanni 1805 und 1806, dazu unveränderlicher Erbzins von 75 Rthl jährlich. Titz trägt alle königlichen Abgaben, die Ląder Klosterabgabe, Rauchfanggeld und Fouragelieferungen, muß selbst bauen, hat Bier- und Branntweinzwang, bei Verkauf Laudemium des zehnten Groschen.
